items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Dan Logan and I were staying together, but Dan didn't drink.

ctx.x: Nassau was not a very large fellow and he must have travelled a lot and had quite a bit of experience before he hit Cincinnati. He played a growl style of trumpet and I wondered many years after where could he have gotten that style, because it was the style of Bubber Miley and Bubber was not known in the middle West of the USA at that time and Duke Ellington was unknown and not recording.

Jessie Smith the alto sax player that had been with the group I was with in Michigan also joined Page's orchestra. The other members were: William Smith, piano, Wilbur Cocksey, alto sax, Page, C melody. Edgar James, drums, and two brothers, Clarence Logan, tuba, and Dan Logan, trombone.. The most outstanding musician in the group was a banjo player named Bob Robinson. Bob came to Cincinnati from West Virginia. I don't know if he was born in that state but that's where he came from when he joined the band. Banjos…

We played regularly at a dance hall at George Street and Central Avenue, which was on the third floor which was called George and Central. It was at that time when a show came to Cincinnati that had a young trumpet player by the name of Cheatham. He came to one of the dances we were playing at George and Central and sat in with us. I could tell right away that he had quite a bit of experience after Bob Robinson. It was usually Nassau that had the biggest success because of his growling, which really did not…
